title: Timed ML Engineering Drills
tools: Python · PyTorch · Hugging Face Transformers and Tokenizers · pytest
blurb: Seven timed practice tasks for ML (machine learning) engineering work: implement, debug and verify against objective tests. Each task has a stub to edit, a pytest suite, and a reference solution; a checker confirms every stub fails and every solution passes, all on CPU (central processing unit) in seconds.
long: I built these drills to practise the kind of paid ML (machine learning) engineering task where code is graded by tests: implement something from a specification, find bugs in a training loop, or match a reference library exactly. Each task has a time budget of 45 to 90 minutes.

The seven tasks: a Llama forward pass from a raw state dict with RMSNorm, RoPE (rotary position embeddings), GQA (grouped-query attention) and a KV (key-value) cache, whose logits must match Hugging Face to 1e-4; numerically stable logsumexp, softmax and cross-entropy on extreme and fp16 inputs; four planted NaN (not-a-number) bugs in a training loop; gradient accumulation with unequal token counts that must match a full-batch step; a byte-level BPE (byte-pair encoding) tokenizer with a chat template and loss mask; bit-exact reproducibility and mid-epoch resume; and batched KV-cached sampling whose top-k, top-p and repetition penalty must equal Hugging Face's.

A small runner tests your work, the reference, or validates every task at once (stub fails, solution passes). The intended workflow is to do each task with a coding agent against the clock and then review the agent's code by hand, since that review is the real skill. GPU-only (graphics processing unit) drills (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp quantization, memory profiling) are written up separately for Colab.
highlights: 7 tasks, 29 tests, each suite under 10 s on a CPU (central processing unit)
Llama forward pass must match Hugging Face logits to 1e-4
Every stub verified failing and every solution passing
